title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
description:
# Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array

Given an integer array `nums` of length `n`, where every value satisfies `1 <= nums[i] <= n`, return all numbers in the range `[1, n]` that do not appear in `nums`.

Return the missing numbers in increasing order. The array may contain duplicates, and a duplicate value can hide one or more other values from the range.

Follow-up: can you solve it in `O(n)` time while using only `O(1)` extra space besides the returned list?

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [4,3,2,7,8,2,3,1]
**Output:** [5,6]
**Explanation:** The values `5` and `6` are the only numbers from `1` through `8` that never appear.

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [1,1]
**Output:** [2]
**Explanation:** The value `1` appears twice, so `2` is missing.

## Example 3:

**Input:** nums = [2,2,2,2]
**Output:** [1,3,4]
**Explanation:** Every slot contains `2`, so all other values in the range `1..4` are missing.

## Constraints:

*   `n == nums.length`
*   `1 <= n <= 10^5`
*   `1 <= nums[i] <= n`

solutions.name: Sign Marking - In-place Hash
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use each value as an index into the same array. For every value `x`, mark index `abs(x) - 1` as negative to record that `x` appears. After all marks, every positive slot `i` means the value `i + 1` was never seen.

## Key Insight

The range guarantee turns the input array into a hash table over `1..n`. Taking `Math.abs` is essential because a duplicate may visit an index that was already marked negative by an earlier value.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1), excluding the returned list

solutions.name: Cyclic Placement
solutions.description:
## Approach

Repeatedly move each value `x` toward index `x - 1`. If the target slot already holds the same value, advance the scan because this value is a duplicate. After placement stops, every index whose value is not `i + 1` identifies a missing number.

## Key Insight

This is the placement form of in-place hashing. The duplicate guard `nums[i] != nums[correctPos]` prevents an infinite swap loop when two equal values want the same target slot.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1), excluding the returned list

solutions.name: Boolean Presence Array
solutions.description:
## Approach

Create a boolean array `seen` indexed by value. Mark every number that appears, then scan candidates from `1` through `n` and collect the positions that were never marked.

## Key Insight

This baseline separates the membership idea from the in-place tricks. It is easier to verify because each candidate has an explicit `seen[candidate]` state.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: HashSet Membership Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach

Insert every array value into a `HashSet`, then check each candidate value from `1` to `n`. Any candidate absent from the set is missing from the input array.

## Key Insight

The set solution is the most direct correctness model: duplicates collapse to one membership entry, and missing values are exactly the candidates whose membership query is false.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
